node-1.label: Patient developed erythema and edematous necrotic plaques of the bilateral ears three days after admission

node-2.label: Patient is a man in his 40s with a medical history of factor VII deficiency hemophilia who presented with acute hypoxic respiratory failure; following admission, he was intubated with prone positioning and treatment was initiated

node-3.label: He was found to have Staphylococcus hemolyticus bacteremia

node-4.label: Three days after admission, the patient developed erythema and edematous necrotic plaques of the bilateral ears; no devices had been used on the ears

node-5.label: The necrosis progressed during the following days, primarily involving the earlobe of the right ear and a large portion of the helix of the left ear; physical exam showed a 2 cm erythematous plaque with overlying eschar on the right earlobe and multiple erythematous edematous erosions with eschar and crust on the helical rim of the left ear

why.why: Pathologist and radiologist analyses confirm that the biopsy shows full-thickness epidermal and dermal necrosis with adnexal necrosis and sparse inflammation, which is consistent with pressure-induced ischemic necrosis. Combined with prone positioning and lesion distribution at pressure points, this strongly supports pressure-induced ear necrosis, raising confidence from 0.6 to 0.8.

Although Staphylococcus hemolyticus bacteremia is present, the biopsy lacks septic vasculitis and vascular thrombi/hemorrhage, and sparse inflammation is atypical for septic emboli. Expert analyses therefore favor pressure-induced necrosis over septic embolic necrosis; tissue culture is still pending, so confidence is lowered from 0.3 to 0.15.

The biopsy lacks vascular thrombi/hemorrhage, and the patient's factor VII deficiency argues against a thrombotic mechanism. Expert analyses conclude that coagulopathic necrosis is improbable, so confidence is lowered from 0.1 to 0.05.
